text:
jordan-rep: Quick ask for a mid-market POC next week. Customer wants minimal human ops during the demo: automatically rotate a hosted demo key every 12 hours, have a webhook notify their demo orchestration when a new key is issued, and automatic revocation after the window. Can we support that with hosted keys?

harper-eng: Short answer: yes, with caveats. Hosted keys can be created/rotated via our API and we emit events in Console Activity + a webhook delivery system. Two main patterns: 1) our rotation API + outbound webhook to customer endpoint, 2) Redwood-managed standby keys with a Secrets Manager push to your vault. Which does the customer prefer?

jordan-rep: They want webhook push (so their demo app can pull the new key and update env). Also need IP allowlist for the demo laptop, rate limiting ~20 r/s, billing tag 'poc/solstice-rotate', and security wants the playbook documented.

samir-sec: Security notes: hosted keys are centrally managed (no per-tenant KMS). Recommend 12h only if the demo automation is reliable; otherwise 24h is safer. Must ensure the webhook uses mutual TLS or a signed JWT to avoid leaking keys to an HTTP endpoint. Also enforce allowlist and scope to chat+embeddings only.

kevin-infra: I can wire a little rotation service for the POC that calls our keys API and posts to the customer's webhook over mTLS. Plan: pre-create a standby key, then every 12h call rotate endpoint which creates a new key, update 1Password + send webhook with key id (not plaintext) and a secure retrieval URL that requires our signed temp token. Customer retrieves plaintext using that signed temp token which expires in 60s. That limits exposure.

harper-eng: Implementation detail: our API supports creating keys and a /keys/:id/issue-temp-token endpoint to mint a short-lived retrieval token. Example flow (curl trimmed):

```
# create key (admin token)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"poc-solstice-rotate","scopes":["chat","embeddings"],"expires_in":43200,"rate_limit":20,"allowlist_ips":["203.0.113.45"],"metadata":{"billing_tag":"poc/solstice-rotate","contact":"demoops@solstice.example.com"}}'

# mint short retrieval token for the newly created key id: <KEY_ID>
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/<KEY_ID>/issue-temp-token \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"ttl":60}'
```

kevin-infra: I'll provide a small node script that runs on our infra side and does: create key -> issue-temp-token -> post webhook {key_id, retrieve_url, expires_at, signed_nonce}. Customer hits retrieve_url once to get plaintext; URL requires the signed_nonce and expires quickly.

samir-sec: Make sure the webhook payload never contains plaintext. Also log the delivery attempt and response code; exportable CSV for audit. For the questionnaire include: webhook delivery logs, Console Activity (create/issue-temp-token/revoke), and the playbook with mTLS/JWT requirements.

jordan-rep: Customer wants to know: will we keep a plaintext copy in our control plane logs or UI? They don't want plaintext hanging around.

harper-eng: We never store plaintext long-term. The control plane stores key metadata and the key material for hosted keys encrypted at rest; but for customers with strict KMS requirements they need Private/Dedicated. For hosted POC keys we can reduce exposure by using the issue-temp-token pattern so plaintext is only retrievable via the short URL and we rotate immediately after retrieval. We'll note that in the playbook.

kevin-infra: Script (pseudo) I'll hand over to you:

```js
// rotate.js (pseudo)
// 1) call create key -> returns key_id
// 2) call issue-temp-token -> returns temp_token + retrieve_url
// 3) post webhook to customer with retrieve_url and expiry (no plaintext)
// 4) poll delivery status, if failed retry x3 then email ops
// 5) after demo revoke key via API
```

jordan-rep: Great. Can you also add a short revocation command and an emergency procedure if the laptop is stolen mid-demo?

harper-eng: Revocation curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/<KEY_ID>/revoke -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'

samir-sec: Emergency steps for playbook: 1) Immediately call revoke endpoint, 2) push new key via rotation service, 3) export Activity CSV and webhook logs, 4) notify customer security contact and Redwood CISO on-call. Include contact emails.

kevin-infra: I'll drop the node script, the webhook TLS cert fingerprint, and a one-page runbook into the deal vault. Also tagging billing as 'poc/solstice-rotate' on creation.

keybot: key created: hosted_key_poc_solstice_rotate_2101234567  created_by: kevin-infra  expires_in: 43200s  scopes: chat, embeddings  rate_limit:20 req/s

jordan-rep: Customer Q: can we automate rotation via the Console (no infra script)?

harper-eng: We have a simple webhook-based automation toggle in Console for early-access accounts. For this POC we can enable it, but it still uses the same issue-temp-token flow under the hood. I'll enable and send screenshot.

keybot: key revoked: hosted_key_poc_solstice_rotate_2101234567  revoked_by: kevin-infra  revocation_time: 2101234890

jordan-rep: Thanks everyone  uploaded the playbook and the logs to the buyer portal and shared the runbook with the customer's security team. They were happy with the no-plaintext webhook design and the emergency revocation steps. :white_check_mark:
